construction.name: coupled_whole_owner_contact_closure
construction.proof:
COUPLED FIRST-ORDER WHOLE-OWNER CONTACT CLOSURE

At a complete fixed-frame packing, give every owner one translation velocity
d_i and give the common host scale a contraction rate delta. At each active
host wall a, require a.d_i + h_host(a)*delta <= 0. At each touching pair i,j,
at least one of its currently realized separating facets a must satisfy
a.(d_j-d_i) >= 0. The same d_i participates in every wall and every contact
incident to owner i. Thus independently successful marginal fans cannot be
combined without satisfying their shared-owner equations.

Solve this finite disjunctive system with |d_i,k|<=1 and 0<=delta<=1. A binary
variable chooses one already-realized facet at each multiple contact; its
big-M bound is 2*||a||_1, which bounds the relative translation response.
This is a finite first-order construction proposal, not a proof that no other
packing or frame exists. Near-contact tolerances may overconstrain it.

If a positive contraction is found, discard the first-order approximation:
retain its chosen physical facets and solve the full common system in actual
owner centers and the actual host scale, including every host wall and every
owner pair. Noncontact pairs retain an already-realized separator. Continue
only through complete feasible predecessors with fixed frames. The final
native exact-input checker, not the mixed-integer solver, certifies the full
packing. Every emitted witness retains the complete native parent, chosen
contact word, shared-owner velocities, all actual common-return rows, and
source marks through the parent decoder.
